Standard: Air vehicle induced engine vibration (e.g., armament firing, inlet or exhaust vibration, AMAD or accessory excitation, APU operation, landing gear transmitted vibration, drive system excitation, propeller or rotary-wing operation/blade passage), including effects of engine mount damping and isolation systems if present, does not exceed engine vibration limits when the engine is operated, at any thrust or power setting (including engine off) under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1 for the stated life documented in engine technical data. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Engine mounting provisions, engine-to-air-vehicle physical interfaces, and engine vibration limits are verified by examination of the ICD. Analysis.
  (1) Design analysis is accomplished to verify vibration transmissibility and engine vibratory response across the engine mount interfaces, and other interfaces capable of transmitting vibration, for any air vehicle-generated forced vibration and impulses. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Ground test confirms that engine vibration limits are not exceeded. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Flight test confirms that engine vibration limits are not exceeded.
